newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -UK share rise prompts mixed option trades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -UK share rise prompts mixed option trades.

text.p: Neutral and spread trades were the main UK stock options deals on Tuesday as the stock market roared ahead, dealers said.
Despite a profits warning from glassmaker Pilkington, one trader bought a neutral-to-bullish calendar spread by selling 1,000 May 120 calls at 8p and buying 1,000 August 120 calls at 11-1/2p.

If the underlying shares are 120p by May expiry, the short calls will be worthless and the long calls will then effectively have been bought for 3-1/2p, so for a profit by August expiry, the shares need to go above 123-1/2p.
At 1501 GMT, Pilkington shares fell 8p to 120-1/2p. The company said pre-tax profits for the year to March 31 would be below market forecasts but not below 130 million stg.
The main deal in diversified industrials group Tomkins was a crossed trade in which 1,000 December 280 puts and calls were traded at 24p and 20p respectively.
In a separate deal, 500 lots in the same series were sold at the same prices in a short straddle strategy which will make a maximum 44p at expiry if the shares are then 280p.
Tomkins shares added a penny to 273p.
Elsewhere, there was a seller of 950 July 140 calls at about 18p in British Steel who stands to make a maximum profit of 18p if the shares go below 140p.
And in banking group Lloyds TSB there was a seller of 725 June 460 puts at 12p. The shares charged up 28p to 482p.
Volatility trades were the main deals in FTSE index options in which options positions are hedged by futures so that market direction is not as important as volatility.
The FTSE 100 index was up 46.6 at 4261.4.
